facts.text: I requested a reduction of the power loss of the previous test 96_20 by using a reduced oil level of -0.5 lt.
I tested the 755/10145957 MF Front Agri axle with reduced oil level (-0.5 lt.) using oil ELF SF3.
I performed a P&T test measuring power loss versus rpm up to 3234 rpm (53 kph) at 90°C and 60°C with ambient temperature 25°C for FWD and REV.
I performed a P&T test at 53 kph FWD to measure power loss and temperature raise.
I performed a lube test with different combinations of speed, direction, and temperatures, including 0° monitoring oil levels in critical areas.
I used reference tests 02_17 (755/611 M2), 05_17 (740/623 M2-19), and 96_20 (755 M2-21 std oil level).
The test was completed without any issue, with no lubrication issues and no oil leak.
In the main results for test 96_20, the power loss versus rpm at 90°C was 3.60 kW (4.55 kW in parentheses).
In the main results for test 96_20, the power loss versus rpm at 60°C was 4.2 kW (5.7 kW in parentheses).
In the main results for test 96_20, the power loss versus rpm at ambient temperature was 8.1 kW (10.3 kW in parentheses) after run-in.
In REV, the power loss was less than in FWD.
In the P&T results, at 1 hr 6 min the central temperature was 85°C and the power loss was 2.8 kW.
In the P&T results, at 2 hours the central temperature was about 110°C and the power loss was 5.3 kW.
In the lube results, at horizontal position there were no signs of lubrication problems and the oil levels in inclined areas were not performed due to not suitable bench availability.
The final tear down was done after the following Hi-speed test 97_20.
The part partially passed the P&T + Lube test because it was improved but had the same power loss step.
In the P&T test, the temperature in the central remained below 120°C (max allowable) within the target 2 hours.
In the P&T test, the power loss step-up became irregular after 1 hr 6 min with no stabilization.
The power loss values were significantly lower than the reference test with the M2 axle and also lower than the 740 axle reference test 05_17.
In the lubrication assessment, the oil level was always above the minimum oil level in all compartments.
I was advised to not reduce the oil level further unless the power loss step-up is solved.
There was no oil leak and no lubrication problem.
The test start date was April 7th, 2021.
The test end date was April 8th, 2021.
The test engineer responsible was Eng. D. Zaglia.
The test location was Off Highway Arco, Italy.
The completion date was June 7th, 2021.
The requestor name was Mr. L. Fornoli.
The test materials included part name 755 with part number 10145957 and revision level Proto 0.
The model series was M2 21V CVT and the sample number was 1.
The axle serial number was C-ITA-374922 and it was Proto1.
The axle was assembled originally at Como and reassembled at Arco after tests 96_21 P&T and 97_21 Hi-speed.
The axle was installed at the test lab with transparent oil tubes for oil level monitoring on both arms, between pinion bearings, and between the pinion tail bearing and seal.
The axle total reduction ratio was 16.79.
The bevel set ratio was 14/37 LH Crown input pinion.
The hub reduction ratio i_hr was 6.353.
There were 4 planetary gears ground to standard production.
The arm seal part number was 10118272 (new Combi-Go).
The input seal part number was 760.04.012.01.
The sun gear cassette seal part number was 10152216.
The wheel hub cassette seal part number was 755.06.082.01.
The oil used was Total Tractelf SF3 (UTTO, DANA first fill).
The central oil quantity was 11.0 -0.5 lt. (below oil level).
The final drives oil quantity was 1.9 lt. each.
The test bench used transparent oil tubes for oil level monitoring and the operator was Giuseppe F.
The calibration data reference file was PRSSTS015011#001BF2.xlsx.
The test procedure used spinning at 53 km/h with horizontal position and FWD direction only.
The wheel radius was 0.73 m and the equivalent input rpm in was 3234 rpm.
The test had no torque/load and no steer.
The axle was in a horizontal position and there was no ventilation.
A temperature probe was placed on the central housing (oil drain plug).
The measured parameters were input speed, differential (drain oil plug) and ambient temperature.
The test cycle ramped speed from max (3234 rpm at pinion) to 0 rpm at ambient temperature 25°C, 60°C, and 90°C with tolerance ±5°C.
Air ventilation was used if necessary with cooling fans to adjust to the desired temperature.
The acceptance criterion for oil temperature was max 120°C oil according to std. DANA Reference TS.30.P&T.A.
The lubrication acceptance criterion was that oil level must not be lower than the lower roller axis so all bearings receive sufficient lubricant amount.
The acceptance criteria included no failure of any components and no leak.
The leak acceptance criterion referenced TS: max level 2 acceptable to SAE J1176.
The acceptance criteria included no sign of overheat or seizure on bearings.
At input speed 3234 rpm in FWD at 25°C, the central temperature was 8.1°C (with power loss 9.4 kW in parentheses).

At input speed 3234 rpm in FWD at 60°C, the central temperature was 110°C with a test time of 120 min and power loss 5.3 kW with a remark of 85°C / 2.8 kW at 60 minutes then power step-up without stabilization (25°C ambient).
At input speed 3234 rpm in FWD at 90°C, the central temperature was 3.6 kW (4.5 kW in parentheses) after run-in.
At input speed 3234 rpm in FWD at 60°C, the power loss was 5.2 kW (5.7 kW in parentheses).
The acquisition for ramp-up used 1 sample / 0.2" = 5 Hz and 1 hr = 18000 samples.
The test bench diagrams used a ramp-up acquisition scale of 5 Hz and 18000 samples per hour.
The P&T diagrams scale was referenced to real axle input speed with a bench in 2nd gear ratio of 1.61 and after post-process off-line graph.
The P vs rpm diagrams scale used axle input rpm multiplied by 1.36.

The lube test included 10 kph and 53 kph speeds in FWD and REV at 20°C, 60°C, and 90°C.
The lube test included a 0° lube test at horizontal position.
The lube test included LH side (Diff.) and RH side (Crown) pinion side.
The lube test photos included 10 kph FWD at 20°C and 10 kph REV at 20°C.
The lube test photos included 53 kph REV at 20°C.
The lube test photos included 10 kph FWD at 60°C and 10 kph REV at 60°C.
The lube test photos included 53 kph FWD at 60°C.
The lube test photos included 10 kph FWD at 90°C (two variants labeled 90°C (1) and 90°C (2)) and 10 kph REV at 90°C.
The lube test photos included 53 kph FWD at 90°C.
The final tear down included a tear down of the central housing.
In the tear down, the pinion tail bearing cup was OK with some dentings probably due to disassembly.
In the tear down, the pinion back-head bearing cup was OK with dragged hard particles marks.
